newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 11.766 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate rises to 11.766 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate jumped to an average of 11.766 percent at Monday's regular weekly auction from 11.562, the Bureau of Treasury said.
Dealers said the persistently high overnight rates triggered the increase in Treasury bill rates.
The 182-day bill edged up to an average of 12.424 from 12.197; and the 364-day bill rose to 12.811 from 12.610.
The auction attracted bids worth only 4.465 billion pesos, of which 3.50 billion pesos were awarded.
"Banks were apprehensive about going in particularly because overnight rates were high," said a trader from a large bank.
"No one knows exactly when it will last. Opinions are varied. Some say the high rates will stay for a few days, while others say it will last a few more weeks," he added.
Dealers said some banks had started to beef up their liquidity positions through the rest of the year in anticipation of the seasonal tightness arising from Christmas spending.
Since last week, rates at the overnight market had risen due to a long weekend covering. Banks were also drained of peso liquidity from their dollar purchases and tax remittances.
The overnight rate nudged up to an average of 14.5625 percent on Monday from 14.53125.
At the T-bill auction, the one-year bills, which had sales of 1.50 billion pesos, generated the most tenders at 2.175 billion pesos.
This was followed by the 182-day bills with 1.245 billion pesos worth of bids, of which 1.0 billion pesos were accepted.
The 91-day bills had bids worth 1.045 billion pesos, of which 1.0 billion pesos were sold.
